comments.body:
REBAR-DEBUG DIAGNOSIS (2026-07-21)

Reproduction/localization: src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py always invokes llm.verify_completion(ticket_id, graph=False, source="attested", ref="HEAD") for a gated non-force close after structural prechecks. src/rebar/llm/reviewers/completion_verifier.md requires every literal acceptance criterion plus the bug-resolution question to be met. It explicitly says a codebase-verifiable criterion is never satisfied by a ticket comment alone.

Root cause: the completion model has only MET/NOT MET over the original criterion text. The lifecycle has no audited "moot/invalidated/superseded criterion" state and no automation-owned alert closure branch. Therefore evidence that disproves the ticket premise cannot reclassify a codebase criterion; it can only fail it, leaving force-close as the sole route.

Minimal corrective seam: introduce an explicit, auditable criterion-disposition/alert-ownership contract before verification, bind it to concrete evidence and authorized provenance, and teach the verifier and close gate to distinguish completed, invalidated/moot, and automation-owned criteria without accepting free-form PASS commands. Regression coverage should include the f436 false-positive alert and reject unsupported moot claims.

No code changed during this diagnostic run.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
FINDINGS (2026-07-24, from closing 620b / 8559 / 86a5)

The gap is NARROWER than this ticket states — one of the three subclasses already has a
working, legitimate close path — but there is also a SECOND stranding gate the ticket does
not mention.

1. `--ref <commit>` IS a legitimate close path for the "ACs invalidated by SUBSEQUENT work"
   subclass, and it works today. Demonstrated on 86a5-9221-0037-4e38: its ACs grep
   `docs/passing-code-review.md`, which a LATER commit (c2bfbe217, "package author guides
   in-package") reduced to a 453-byte pointer stub. Closing at worktree HEAD would have been
   judged against a tree where the criteria are unsatisfiable. Closing with
   `--ref f90850861` (the commit the work actually landed in) verified against the tree the
   ACs were written for and PASSED — signed, no --force-close, no AC edit. This is the
   correct escape hatch for this subclass and it should be documented as such in the close
   workflow, not reinvented.

   Note the flag already exists on BOTH surfaces: `rebar transition ... closed --ref <c>`
   (`_commands/transition.py:165-171`, both `--ref X` and `--ref=X`) and library
   `transition(..., ref=...)`, and it is documented at `docs/cli-reference.md:393`.

2. `--ref` does NOT solve the other two subclasses this ticket names:
   (a) ACs invalidated BY THE FIX ITSELF — there is no ref at which both the fix is present
       and the original criteria are satisfiable; the two are mutually exclusive by
       construction. This is the genuinely unaddressed case.
   (b) AUTO-GENERATED / UNVERIFIABLE ACs — bad at every ref, so no ref selection helps.
   (c) AUTOMATION-OWNED alert tickets (the originating f436-fac8-382f-47ec case) — closure is
       owned by the filing automation, not by a code-verifiable criterion.

3. NEW — a SECOND gate strands finished work, and it is expensive. Closing 86a5 first failed
   on the PLAN-REVIEW close gate, not the completion verifier:

       plan-review close gate: stale-regver: the criteria registry changed since the plan
       review (overlay activated/edited/disabled). Health: legacy-unpinned (enforced)

   The ticket's plan review was signed under rebar 0.8.0; the criteria registry has since
   changed, so a ticket whose CODE WORK IS DONE AND MERGED could not close until a full
   billable `rebar review-plan --force` re-review of its (already-executed) plan was run.
   Re-reviewing a plan that has already shipped, purely to satisfy a registry-version check,
   is the same class of defect as this ticket: a gate with no legitimate path for a ticket
   whose work is genuinely complete. Whatever disposition contract comes out of this ticket
   should cover the plan-review close gate too, not just the completion verifier.

4. This ticket has NO Acceptance Criteria section of its own. That must be fixed before it
   can be worked — as written, the completion verifier would auto-generate criteria for it,
   which is precisely the failure mode the ticket exists to fix.

RECOMMENDED SCOPE after these findings:
- Document `--ref <landing-commit>` as the sanctioned close path for the invalidated-by-later-
  work subclass (cheapest win; the mechanism already ships).
- Design the auditable criterion-disposition record (moot / invalidated-by-fix / superseded)
  bound to cited evidence + authorized provenance, for subclass (a).
- Add an automation-owned closure branch for bot-filed alert tickets, for subclass (c).
- Extend whatever disposition contract results to the plan-review close gate's stale-regver
  path, so completed work is not forced through a re-review of an already-executed plan.

Moving back to OPEN: the ticket was `in_progress` with no assignee and no live claim session
(a stale claim), and it now needs a plan + ACs before any implementation.

compiled_state.description:
Distinct from eaa9 (supersedes/duplicates awareness). This gap: the completion-verification close gate requires EVERY acceptance criterion to be met as literally written, with the only escapes being --force-close (a bypass) or the idea->closed hack. It has NO legitimate author-driven path for two real cases:

1. ACs INVALIDATED BY THE FIX. When the correct fix proves the reported premise false (a false-positive reclassification), the original ACs become unsatisfiable-by-correct-design, yet the verifier still demands they be met. There is no way to record 'this criterion is moot because the fix reclassified the premise, here is the evidence' — and because the criteria are codebase-verifiable, an attestation COMMENT is explicitly rejected.

2. BOT-AUTHORED ALERT tickets carry AUTO-GENERATED ACs (triage templates) that assume the alert condition is real and actionable. When it isn't (false positive) or when closure is owned by an automation (the canary force-closes bot alerts by design), the human/author completion path can never pass.

REPRO: bug f436-fac8-382f-47ec — a rebar-bridge[bot] binding-drift alert. Its ACs ('each reported drift is triaged', 'bridge-fsck reports empty binding_drift') assume the 163 dangling entries were real. The merged fix (Gerrit 848) proved them FALSE POSITIVES (alive aged-out bindings); live bridge-fsck shows 0 actionable drift. The verifier still FAILs the close ('2 unmet criteria') and rejects the live-evidence comment as insufficient for codebase-verifiable criteria. The only closes available are the canary's own --force-close or a manual force-close.

EXPECTED: a legitimate, audited author path to close when ACs are demonstrably moot/invalidated (with cited evidence the verifier accepts), and/or a first-class notion of bot-authored alert tickets whose closure is owned by their filing automation and not subject to author-completion verification. Same 'lifecycle requirement not propagated to a legitimate branch' family as eaa9 / ed13 / 0e15.

Discovered during the rebar-debug batch while trying to close f436 after its fix landed.
compiled_state.title: Completion verifier has no legitimate close path when acceptance criteria are invalidated by the fix or are auto-generated/unverifiable
